source_1: Schwarz et al. 2023, Redox Biol 59:102593, PMID 36608588, doi 10.1016/j.redox.2022.102593 (full text PMC9827380, read through the PubMed connector 24 November 2026; recombinant human GPX1, GPX2 and GPX4, glutathione-reductase-coupled NADPH assay, each hydroperoxide at 50 uM): 15(S)-HpEPE (Table 1, Cayman 42710) was a substrate; "both GPX1 and GPX4 were able to reduce these five substrates, and GPX1 again showed higher efficiency" (the five: 5S-, 12S- and 15S-HpEPE, 15S-HpEDE, 17S-HpDHA); the product was identified: "the corresponding monohydroxylated fatty acids of 9S-HpODE, 13S-HpODE, 12-HpETE, 15S-HpEPE, and 17S-HpDHA were quantified by UPLC ... source_2: Archambault et al. 2018, PLoS One 13:e0202424, PMID 30118527 (another laboratory; full text XML PMC6097673 read on Europe PMC 24 November 2026, CC BY 4.0): "The treatment of neutrophils and eosinophils with linoleic acid, dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid, arachidonic acid, eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid and arachidonyl-ethanolamide, led to the synthesis of 13-HODE, 15-HETrE, 15-HETE, 15-HEPE, 14-HDHA/17-HDHA, and 15-hydroxy-AEA": the hydroxy acid is what human cells make from EPA through a 15-lipoxygenase, so it is the product of the step and not its substrate. The paper does not discuss the hydroperoxide or its reductant (searched for hydroperox, peroxidase, reduc); the reductant rests on source_1
note: Exact substrate measured, product identified by UPLC-MS/MS. Upstream rewrote this reaction the same way on its develop branch (issue #1173, pull request #1177, in no release as of 24 November 2026), citing RHEA:76707 and grading it "moderate: Rhea of an analogue substrate"; RHEA:76707 is this substrate, not an analogue. In the pinned model the hydroperoxide is made by a lipoxygenase (MAR02558 from 15(R)-HpEPE) and this reaction is its only link to the hydroxy acid, written reversible with the hydroxy acid as nominal substrate, +2 in charge (computed from the pinned formulas and charges), so the graph's edges run from product to precursor. Human-GEM 2.1.1 still holds the pinned equation.

No hydroperoxide of an eicosatrienoate was among the 17 substrates. The two 15(S)-hydroperoxides nearest to it were: 15(S)-HpETE (the tetraenoate, reduced by all three enzymes) and 15(S)-HpEDE (the 11Z,13E-dienoate; "both GPX1 and GPX4 were able to reduce these five substrates"). The class reaction is RHEA:19057, "a hydroperoxy polyunsaturated fatty acid + 2 glutathione = a hydroxy polyunsaturated fatty acid + glutathione disulfide + H2O", EC 1.11.1.12, on UniProt P07203 and P36969 (flat files read 24 November 2026)
source_2: Archambault et al. 2018, PLoS One 13:e0202424, PMID 30118527 (another laboratory; full text XML PMC6097673 read on Europe PMC 24 November 2026, CC BY 4.0): "The treatment of neutrophils and eosinophils with linoleic acid, dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid, arachidonic acid, eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid and arachidonyl-ethanolamide, led to the synthesis of 13-HODE, 15-HETrE, 15-HETE, 15-HEPE, 14-HDHA/17-HDHA, and 15-hydroxy-AEA"; and Iversen et al. 1991, Agents Actions 33:286, PMID 1659156 (a third laboratory, ABSTRACT ONLY, PubMed record read 24 November 2026): human neutrophils given dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid show "a dose dependent increase in the formation of the respective 15-LO products of LA (13-hydroxy-octadecadienoic acid; 13-HODE) and DGLA (15-hydroxy-eicosatrienoic acid; 15-HETrE)". So the hydroxy acid is the product. Neither names the hydroperoxide's reductant
note: The weakest of the three: the direction and the product rest on two laboratories, the glutathione peroxidases on the class reaction and on the tetraenoate and dienoate neighbours, as the accepted 15(R)-HEPE rows rest on the 15(S) analogue. Upstream rewrote this reaction the same way on its develop branch (issue #1173, pull request #1177, in no release as of 24 November 2026) with the gene rule of MAR00960. In the pinned model the hydroperoxide is made by a lipoxygenase (MAR01388, ALOX15 or ALOX15B) and this reaction is its only link to the hydroxy acid, written reversible with the hydroxy acid as nominal substrate, +2 in charge (computed from the pinned formulas and charges), so the graph's edges run from product to precursor. Human-GEM 2.1.1 still holds the pinned equation.
